title: gsm_sim: Detect Le byte on an unknown command type
description:
If we have a nonzero P3 byte with at least that length
of data following it (= Lc + Data), and then there's one
more byte present past that, it is Le. Possibly not if this is
a GSMTAP capture from SIMtrace + SIMtrace2, which always
combines the command and response APDUs into one packet:
https://github.com/yarrick/scsniff/issues/1#issuecomment-2295835330

Ping #20115

notes.body:
> and then there's one more byte present past that, it is Le

Correction:\
Le might be up to 3 bytes, please see the table:\
https://github.com/estkme-group/lpac/issues/118 \
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_card_application_protocol_data_unit#APDU_message_command-response_pair

So I think the easiest way to deduce Le in GSMTAP capture is to see if there are more than 3 bytes past the data:
- if that's the case, it's pending for further deduction
- otherwise, it's Le, for sure

That table claims to be for ISO/IEC 7816, but ETSI TS 102 221 (https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/102200_102299/102221/18.00.00_60/ts_102221v180000p.pdf) indicates that Le can only be one byte. So what you propose might be appropriate for the IOS 7816 dissector instead.
OK, I hope user would be able to choose the dissector, then (I don't know if we can always do it automatically properly).

suggestions.from_content:
proto_tree_add_item(sim_tree, hf_le, tvb, offset, 1, ENC_NA);
				offset += 1;
suggestions.to_content:
proto_tree_add_item(sim_tree, hf_le, tvb, offset, tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, offset), ENC_NA);
				offset += tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, offset);

notes.body: ETSI TS 102 221 is clear in several places that it does not implement everything in ISO/IEC  ISO/IEC 7816 and expressly deviates in a few. I imagine that's part of why there's two separate dissectors.

Then the question arises (probably a separate topic):\
can we deduce proper dissector for the given trace somehow?

One strange thing I noticed: \
For chained GSM SIM commands to device ("Block chaining: More blocks"), we still have Le byte set (00):
![image](/uploads/915f4df2ec7d0ce307c85ad290495cf9/image.png){width=900 height=272}

This apparently contradicts to [ISO/IEC 7816](https://github.com/estkme-group/lpac/issues/118#issuecomment-2169637432), which demands "Le field shall be absent" in this case (not sure where is "b5" bit here, though). \
Am I missing something?

PS: \
Followup question - what are the last 3 bytes here, then (00 4d 00)?

@stigbjorlykke

The last 00 byte is included in the Response Length, so I would guess this was added when capturing. Wireshark tries to display as best as possible here, maybe it should give warning in this case? It does not belong in the APDU payload because that is 255 bytes.

The last 3 bytes 004d00 look like padding, but then they should all be 00. Someone with MBIM knowledge could maybe answer this.

> The last 3 bytes 004d00 look like padding, but then they should all be 00.

They are in some other packets in the same capture:
![image](/uploads/0f8ad6edba68a30d79e298c45aa5a654/image.png){width=900 height=288}

So it's something odd happening here. \
The other possibility is Windows MBIM implementation doesn't quite follow the standard.

Overall, the presence/absence of Le field can have huge impact on practice, up to denying the eSIM card to work: \
https://github.com/estkme-group/lpac/issues/118

So yes, even if we don't know the truth yet, it would be good if we at least show a warning if the Le field is unexpectedly missing or present (this case) according to the standard.
I created !23517 to show the padding bytes.

> According to the GlobalPlatform Card Specification the last 00 byte should not be present when more blocks expected.

And also the Le _should_ be present when it's the last block, so it worth the warning if it doesn't, too. \
As it is exact problem which made eSIM non-functional with lpac on the link above (we don't see this case in my capture because it was done for Windows-native MBIM communication instead).
Yes, this will show as a generic "out of data" error. I'll have a look at making this a better warning.
Thanks. Maybe specify the Le doesn't comply with particular standard and why.
